blocks.text: This page tracks the North Vancouver MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $1,281,400 for a typical home, down 2.7% over twelve months.
North Vancouver benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical North Vancouver home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,281,400 in October 2026. That is little changed at −0.7% on the month, down 2.0% over three months, down 2.9% over six months and down 2.7% over the year. Over three years it is down 6.5%, and over five years little changed at −0.2%.
The weakest one-year move in North Vancouver was for an apartment homes at −6.1%; the strongest was a detached home at −2.2%.
The gap between a detached home ($2,058,800) and an apartment ($736,300) is $1,322,500, and a townhouse ($1,221,100) sits $484,800 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, North Vancouver is 19.9% above. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against down 2.7% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, North Vancouver ranks 4 by all-home benchmark, with Whistler above it at $1,359,000 and Vancouver West below it at $1,196,600.

Detached homes in North Vancouver: benchmark $2,058,800, little changed at +0.8% in a month, little changed at −0.9% in three months, down 3.3% in six months, down 2.2% in a year, down 7.5% in three years and little changed at −0.2% in five. That is 16.0% above the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in North Vancouver: benchmark $1,221,100, little changed at −0.8% in a month, little changed at −1.3% in three months, down 4.1% in six months, down 5.9% in a year, down 9.2% in three years and up 2.4% in five. That is 21.3% above the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in North Vancouver: benchmark $736,300, down 4.3% in a month, down 6.3% in three months, down 6.2% in six months, down 6.1% in a year, down 8.9% in three years and up 3.2% in five. That is 9.3% above the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical North Vancouver home is worth about $35,600 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,317,000. By type, detached homes lost about $46,300, from $2,105,100 to $2,058,800, townhouses lost about $76,600, from $1,297,700 to $1,221,100, and apartments lost about $47,800, from $784,100 to $736,300 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $1,319,700 six months ago and near $1,370,500 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $38,300 below the six-month mark and about $89,100 below the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the North Vancouver benchmark is about $212,800 above the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $189,800 above.
What the North Vancouver figure is
The $1,281,400 North Vancouver figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for October 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in North Vancouver?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical North Vancouver home was $1,281,400, with detached at $2,058,800.

faq.q: Are North Vancouver home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: North Vancouver is down 2.7% over twelve months and down 2.0% over three months.
